title: Kink Band Structure in BCC HEAs and In-situ Observation of Its Evolution During Plastic Deformation
content: Recently, body-centered cubic (bcc) refractory multicomponent alloys (MEA) composed of Group IV, V, and VI elements have demonstrated significant potential as structural materials under extreme temperature environments [1-4] because of their high melting points, and ability to retain excellent compression strength under high temperatures [3]. However, their practical applications remain limited due to their high ductile to brittle transition temperatures, low tensile ductility and damage tolerance ability at room temperature [2, 5]. Kink bands, a deformation mechanism that reorients crystals into favorable slip directions, has emerged as a promising approach to enhance plasticity and subsequently damage tolerance in these alloys [6]. Specifically, this mechanism has been attributed to the remarkably high toughness of a recently discovered Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 (NTTH) bcc HEA. Experimental observation indicates that these bands are formed through activation of multiple slip systems (Fig. 1).
